title: Choose the visual world for Whenever
question: The roll assigned the enamel street sign. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Enamel street sign
options.lineage: Indian municipal enamel street and house-number plates
options.thesis: Every Whenever is a fired-enamel plate, its sentence set like a street name you read from across the road.
options.viewport: Cobalt top bar, then My Whenevers as a stack of enamel plates: white sentence on cobalt, a green THEN sub-plate with the actions, a red tab when one fired.
options.risk: Reads as heritage signage if the type turns decorative; the plates must stay plain cards with standard controls.

raised.raise: Hierarchy by scale contrast alone: the sentence is the largest thing on every screen, labels stay small.
One type family throughout, set on a hairline grid.
Activity keeps guide words: the time span in view stays pinned at the top while you scroll.
One ink is reserved: signal red appears only when something fired.

options.label: Gate visitor register
options.lineage: the visitor register at every Indian gate and reception desk
options.thesis: Every event is a row in the register: time, camera, what happened, and the proof that signs it.
options.viewport: Activity first: rows of time, camera, event and a proof thumbnail, with a violet CHECKED stamp on verified rows.
options.risk: The most familiar idea for a security product, and ruled paper can turn into a costume of a ledger.

options.label: Midnight transit diagram
options.lineage: metro maps fired as enamel murals
options.thesis: Each Whenever is a line from its trigger station to its action stations.
options.viewport: My Whenevers as coloured lines: Gate wide, car blocks 5 min, then Phone and Gate light as stations.
options.case: Fuses well: if-then maps cleanly to a route and holds clarity, but a map form strains Create and Actions.
options.risk: A map on every screen gets dense; it must stay one signature move, never the layout.

options.label: Vertical proof feed
options.thesis: Each alert fills the phone with its proof frame, and the next alert is one flick away.
options.viewport: Activity: a full-screen frame of a car at the gate, caption low left, a rail of Right, Wrong, Light and Share on the right.
options.case: Fuses well for alert review on a phone and for operators, but it carries nothing for Create or Actions.
options.risk: Strong on Activity only; the rest of the app borrows nothing from it.

options.label: Variable type specimen
options.thesis: Rules as letterforms that morph under a slider.
options.viewport: One giant sentence with axis sliders.
options.case: Fuses poorly: owners and operators do not identify with a type foundry.
options.risk: Becomes a type demo, not a camera tool.

options.label: Design annual plates
options.thesis: Proof frames as printed plates with registration marks.
options.viewport: Proof frames in a hairline grid with a stamp.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a print annual is far from a gate or a café.
options.kept: One type family on a hairline grid.
options.risk: Precious and quiet where alerts need urgency.

options.label: Lexicon page
options.thesis: Rules as dictionary entries with guide words.
options.viewport: A column of rule entries with guide words.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a reading form for a tool people operate.
options.kept: Guide words that name the span in view.
options.risk: Bookish and slow on a phone.

options.label: Orienteering map
options.thesis: Cameras as terrain with the active rule in purple.
options.viewport: A terrain map with purple course legs.
options.case: Fuses poorly: camera views are not terrain.
options.kept: One ink reserved for the active state.
options.risk: Pretty but hard to read at a glance.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What IFTTT-style automation apps ship, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A white list of rule cards with coloured service tiles and big pill buttons.
